commander_identity.mechanical_plan: Cast Admiral Beckett Brass for {1}{U}{B}{R}; connect with three different Pirates against the same opponent, then use Admiral's beginning-endstep ability to gain control of an eligible nonland permanent. Repeat through cheap evasive Pirates, recurring blocker disruption and on-hit draw/treasure.
commander_identity.natural_ceiling: Power Bracket 4 — Optimized: persistent multiplayer permanent theft and combat-value Pirate swarm, with interaction, tutors and valuable back-up combat damage. Requires three distinct combat connections, stable commander and legal endstep targets; not forced into generic cEDH.
commander_identity.anti_homogenization: Retain Pirates, evasion, recurring Daring Piracy entries, Merchant Raiders lockdown, The Indomitable combat draw, Open into Wonder card flow and stolen-permanent synergies; avoid replacing unique theft identity with unrelated Grixis goodstuff or noncombat storm.

whole_deck_audit.roles_and_overlaps: Reopened all 99 noncommander slots, not just preselected additions: 35 lands and color access; 34 creature cards, 33 Pirate/changeling bodies; cheap attackable flight, menace, conditional evasion, Daring Piracy and recurring entries; Admiral exact 3 distinct Pirates damaging one opponent; on-hit draw, Treasure, tutoring, protection, repeatable locking, counterspells, instant/sorcery removal, theft endstep and recursion. 65 nonlands MV1–MV5 histogram 9/23/15/12/6, mean ~2.74. Seven actual source-bound complete 100-card configurations tested source and finite mechanics; higher-swap options explored because five is not a stopping point.
whole_deck_audit.mana_base_and_curve: New six-change physical list preserves 35 lands and 34 creatures; 97 distinct names (3 Islands, 2 Mountains, 1 Swamp), rest singleton. Five four- and five-mana engine slots preserved deliberately. City instead of mandatory-tapped Necropolis aids the actual UBR fourth-land commander line at one damage per tap. Cosmotronic Wave {3}{R} replaces Raise the Palisade {4}{U}, retains Fiery Cannonade {2}{R} instant and Open into Wonder XUU (X=3 costs {3}{U}{U}); frozen Scryfall Oracle source verifies Grixis color pips. Typed fetch lands and generic effects do not waive the actual costs.
whole_deck_audit.interaction_resilience: Retain reactive instant Fiery Cannonade's two damage to each non-Pirate creature, which a sorcery-speed offensive Wave cannot replicate. Merchant Raiders provides repeat tapping; Open into Wonder creates X true unblockable attackers and on-hit card draw; Bident, The Indomitable and Kindred Discovery are repeat card access, and black sorcery March of the Drowned recovers Pirates. Toxic Deluge, Chaos Warp, Cyclonic Rift, Mana Drain, Fierce Guardianship and Deflecting Swat cover opposing attacks and target interaction. Flying/reach blockers, Fog, spell responses, removal before endstep, and Wave's nonlasting one-turn unblock expose real counterplay.

weakest_slots.weakness: A guaranteed-tapped three-color land postpones four-mana Admiral when drawn as the fourth source; its painless fixing can still be useful in a slow game.
weakest_slots.reasoning: Swap an always-tapped source for immediate UBR access while transparently accepting City's every-tap triggered self-damage.

weakest_slots.weakness: Pirate's recurring evasion requires 2U each combat and can conflict with casting and protecting the commander, although combat loot is genuine.
weakest_slots.reasoning: Deckhand is already hard to block against non-Spirits for the same printed {1}{U} and pays for another creature only when needed; removal-spell targeting is a downside.

weakest_slots.weakness: Ground-based attacker scales power when other Pirates attack but does not secure the third distinct hit that Beckett counts.
weakest_slots.reasoning: Move a source into the first-turn flying slot; losing ground defense and attack-scaling damage is a deliberate commander-first tradeoff.

weakest_slots.weakness: Flash deathtouch gives useful instant-speed trading and attacking-Pirate combat trick but does not inherently evade blockers as a third source.
weakest_slots.reasoning: Skyship flies over ground blockers and adds existing counters on a hit, including a verified conditional Malcolm chorus line; weaker against flyers and reach.

weakest_slots.weakness: Three-mana topdeck Pirate tutor and repeated noncombat each-opponent Pirate-entry drain are valuable but do not themselves produce a same-player three-Pirate hit.
weakest_slots.reasoning: Haste/menace yields immediate attacking Pirate pressure and paid postattack removal; forfeits true tutor/attrition capacity, especially repeated Daring Piracy tokens.

weakest_slots.weakness: Four-mana body delays immediate offense and may die to removal; competing Blustersquall can tap every opposing creature at instant speed once.
weakest_slots.reasoning: Retain Raiders for repeating Pirate-entry tap that keeps blockers frozen while it survives; a one-turn all-blocker tap gives up core permanent-theft support.

weakest_slots.weakness: Four-mana non-Pirate Vehicle competes with developing early Pirates and can be stranded when behind on board.
weakest_slots.reasoning: Retain this uncrewed passive per-combat-hit draw engine and conditional graveyard reuse; replacing it with one-shot tap sacrifices game-long card access.

weakest_slots.weakness: An XUU sorcery consumes five mana and two blue to unblock three creatures, exposing it to reactive spells and mana bottlenecks.
weakest_slots.reasoning: Retain guaranteed unblockable targeting and actual on-hit draw when X=3; War Cadence is a paid repeated tax opponents may pay and removes the card reward.

weakest_slots.weakness: Cheap recursion can be small after a multi-creature wipe and may be a narrow late topdeck.
weakest_slots.reasoning: Retain the flexible one-Pirate or two-Pirate recovery in a mixed table rather than a five-mana symmetrical tribal rebirth that often aids opponents.

weakest_slots.weakness: Five-mana creature temporarily borrows a hand creature rather than directly guaranteeing a Pirate damage source; attack timing is fragile.
weakest_slots.reasoning: Retain repeatable Pirate-themed temporary opposing-hand theft; Kindred Charge is six mana, needs an already-wide board, and loses legendary copies to legend rule.

weakest_slots.weakness: Expensive legend consumes upper curve and is weak when the graveyard has few Pirates.
weakest_slots.reasoning: Keep actual Pirate recovery and named Admiral identity rather than a symmetrical burst of exile-bound copies that cannot fix an empty board.

weakest_slots.weakness: Always enters tapped and can delay an on-curve four-mana commander despite future Pirate-cast scry.
weakest_slots.reasoning: Keep UBR commander-colored production and on-type scry; colorless Access Tunnel plus three-mana activation is too expensive for a deck already demanding UBR.

weakest_slots.weakness: Palisade is a five-mana sorcery type-conditional mass bounce; naming Pirate allows opposing Pirate blockers to stay on board.
weakest_slots.reasoning: Select cheaper Wave because it prohibits blockers of ALL opposing types on theft-combat turn; acknowledge losing lasting bounce and defense.

weakest_slots.weakness: Two damage against non-Pirates sometimes misses big flyers and does not clear Pirate blockers, but responds instantly to non-Pirate aggression.
weakest_slots.reasoning: Full six-change Wave-for-Cannonade alternative sacrifices distinct instant response; retain Cannonade, cut Palisade.

weakest_slots.weakness: The created Ragavan Monkey token does not qualify as one of the three distinct Pirates dealing damage for Admiral.
weakest_slots.reasoning: Aerialist's aerial third-hit opportunity is real but raid setup and losing Kari's first strike, menace and token combat value reduce resilience.

weakest_slots.weakness: Four-mana artifact has no evasion effect and risks low immediate payoff when nobody gets through.
weakest_slots.reasoning: Regalia protects and evades one body while sacrificing Bident's repeatable draw for every connecting Pirate across combat.

whole_deck_audit.current_baseline_strength: Locked approved baseline is coherent Pirate theft with Forerunner tutor plus Pirate-entry drain, Poisoner flash/deathtouch, Captain scaling attacker, Saboteur loot, Raise the Palisade lasting tribal bounce and three protected distinct draw engines. These are meaningful sacrifices; the sixth swap specifically exchanges five-mana type-limited Palisade bounce for four-mana unconditional same-turn no-block Wave, not a cosmetic quota filler.
whole_deck_audit.candidate_pool_scope: Existing M5 and 62-deck Pass C (waived non-independent reviewer), original 24 candidate dispositions, EDHREC top-inclusion and High Lift off-list leads, 28 material dispositions and 16 incumbent roles, original A/B/C/D and NEW exact complete 100 six-, seven- and nine-change competing packages. Finite payable-cost, effects and board tests; no claim that a source-bound I/J proves a global multiplayer best.
whole_deck_audit.off_ranked_search_conclusion: OFF-RANKING discovery added full Oracle-checked Cosmotronic Wave and EDHREC High Lift Pirate options (especially Aerialist, Dreamcaller, Kitesail Corsair, Deadeye Brawler, Prying Blade) plus Brotherhood Regalia. Their prevalence and lift determine scouting priority, not inclusion. Seven- and nine-swap variants lose important defensive, draw or guaranteed X=3 unblock roles and were rejected on whole-100 opportunity cost.

final_changes.coherent_package_tradeoff: Six independently justified commander-first replacements: instant-access City for tapped Necropolis; untaxed passive-evasion Deckhand for Saboteur's costly loot/evasion; one-drop flying Cloud Pirates for ground-scaling Captain; Skyship flying counter synergy for Poisoner's flash combat trick; haste/menace Broadside for Forerunner's tutor/drain; universal same-turn four-mana Cosmotronic Wave against five-mana type-conditional Palisade bounce. Retain instant defensive Fiery Cannonade, Open's X=3 unblock/draw, Bident/Indomitable/Discovery repeated draw, March recursion. Lose lasting bounce, tutoring, ground damage, instant deathtouch and City's self-damage risk. Seven- and nine-change coherent 100-card alternatives were directly evaluated without aiming for a number.

weakest_slot_challenge.weakness: A guaranteed-tapped three-color land postpones four-mana Admiral when drawn as the fourth source; its painless fixing can still be useful in a slow game.
weakest_slot_challenge.reasoning: Swap an always-tapped source for immediate UBR access while transparently accepting City's every-tap triggered self-damage.

weakest_slot_challenge.weakness: Pirate's recurring evasion requires 2U each combat and can conflict with casting and protecting the commander, although combat loot is genuine.
weakest_slot_challenge.reasoning: Deckhand is already hard to block against non-Spirits for the same printed {1}{U} and pays for another creature only when needed; removal-spell targeting is a downside.

weakest_slot_challenge.weakness: Ground-based attacker scales power when other Pirates attack but does not secure the third distinct hit that Beckett counts.
weakest_slot_challenge.reasoning: Move a source into the first-turn flying slot; losing ground defense and attack-scaling damage is a deliberate commander-first tradeoff.

weakest_slot_challenge.weakness: Flash deathtouch gives useful instant-speed trading and attacking-Pirate combat trick but does not inherently evade blockers as a third source.
weakest_slot_challenge.reasoning: Skyship flies over ground blockers and adds existing counters on a hit, including a verified conditional Malcolm chorus line; weaker against flyers and reach.

weakest_slot_challenge.weakness: Three-mana topdeck Pirate tutor and repeated noncombat each-opponent Pirate-entry drain are valuable but do not themselves produce a same-player three-Pirate hit.
weakest_slot_challenge.reasoning: Haste/menace yields immediate attacking Pirate pressure and paid postattack removal; forfeits true tutor/attrition capacity, especially repeated Daring Piracy tokens.

weakest_slot_challenge.weakness: Four-mana body delays immediate offense and may die to removal; competing Blustersquall can tap every opposing creature at instant speed once.
weakest_slot_challenge.reasoning: Retain Raiders for repeating Pirate-entry tap that keeps blockers frozen while it survives; a one-turn all-blocker tap gives up core permanent-theft support.

weakest_slot_challenge.weakness: Four-mana non-Pirate Vehicle competes with developing early Pirates and can be stranded when behind on board.
weakest_slot_challenge.reasoning: Retain this uncrewed passive per-combat-hit draw engine and conditional graveyard reuse; replacing it with one-shot tap sacrifices game-long card access.

weakest_slot_challenge.weakness: An XUU sorcery consumes five mana and two blue to unblock three creatures, exposing it to reactive spells and mana bottlenecks.
weakest_slot_challenge.reasoning: Retain guaranteed unblockable targeting and actual on-hit draw when X=3; War Cadence is a paid repeated tax opponents may pay and removes the card reward.

weakest_slot_challenge.weakness: Cheap recursion can be small after a multi-creature wipe and may be a narrow late topdeck.
weakest_slot_challenge.reasoning: Retain the flexible one-Pirate or two-Pirate recovery in a mixed table rather than a five-mana symmetrical tribal rebirth that often aids opponents.

weakest_slot_challenge.weakness: Five-mana creature temporarily borrows a hand creature rather than directly guaranteeing a Pirate damage source; attack timing is fragile.
weakest_slot_challenge.reasoning: Retain repeatable Pirate-themed temporary opposing-hand theft; Kindred Charge is six mana, needs an already-wide board, and loses legendary copies to legend rule.

weakest_slot_challenge.weakness: Expensive legend consumes upper curve and is weak when the graveyard has few Pirates.
weakest_slot_challenge.reasoning: Keep actual Pirate recovery and named Admiral identity rather than a symmetrical burst of exile-bound copies that cannot fix an empty board.

weakest_slot_challenge.weakness: Always enters tapped and can delay an on-curve four-mana commander despite future Pirate-cast scry.
weakest_slot_challenge.reasoning: Keep UBR commander-colored production and on-type scry; colorless Access Tunnel plus three-mana activation is too expensive for a deck already demanding UBR.

weakest_slot_challenge.weakness: Palisade is a five-mana sorcery type-conditional mass bounce; naming Pirate allows opposing Pirate blockers to stay on board.
weakest_slot_challenge.reasoning: Select cheaper Wave because it prohibits blockers of ALL opposing types on theft-combat turn; acknowledge losing lasting bounce and defense.

weakest_slot_challenge.weakness: Two damage against non-Pirates sometimes misses big flyers and does not clear Pirate blockers, but responds instantly to non-Pirate aggression.
weakest_slot_challenge.reasoning: Full six-change Wave-for-Cannonade alternative sacrifices distinct instant response; retain Cannonade, cut Palisade.

weakest_slot_challenge.weakness: The created Ragavan Monkey token does not qualify as one of the three distinct Pirates dealing damage for Admiral.
weakest_slot_challenge.reasoning: Aerialist's aerial third-hit opportunity is real but raid setup and losing Kari's first strike, menace and token combat value reduce resilience.

weakest_slot_challenge.weakness: Four-mana artifact has no evasion effect and risks low immediate payoff when nobody gets through.
weakest_slot_challenge.reasoning: Regalia protects and evades one body while sacrificing Bident's repeatable draw for every connecting Pirate across combat.

open_ended_optimization_audit.remaining_99_review: We inspected all 99 legal main-deck slots after the five-change gate: 35 lands/color sources; fast Pirate deployment and conditioned mana access, every cheap Pirate's actual evasion and subtype; Treasure, repeated token entries, combo/payoff slots, tutor effects, commander-safe three-different-Pirate connections; counterspells, protection, instant versus sorcery mass responses, Pirate recursion, on-hit multi-card draw, removal and theft endstep constraints. Additional seventh/ninth swaps were built as actual 100s instead of assuming five was optimal. Kari, Bident, Open, Cannonade, March and Path retain differentiated jobs.

post_floor_challenges.tradeoff: High-lift aerial Pirate adds a flying distinct damage source after raid, but Kari herself is a Pirate with first strike and menace and creates a separately attacking Ragavan Monkey token. That token is not a Pirate yet still gives combat utility; conditional raid and lost defense make Aerialist a meta choice.

Regalia equips to protect/evade one Pirate at substantial tempo cost. Bident generates a card for each creature dealing combat damage, scaling with the three qualifying Pirates Admiral needs, so dropping the multi-hit engine for one evasive card is a quality loss.

Siren can flash-tap two nonlands if another Pirate exists but cannot join same-turn attack without haste. Open for X=3 costs five mana for three creatures that cannot be blocked and up to three on-hit draws, directly synchronizing Admiral's target-player theft threshold.

larger_swap_packages.case_for_extra_swaps: Source-bound seven-replacement list gains one more aerial Pirate over Kari Zev on top of six commander-first improvements; EDHREC High Lift suggests that ground-blocked pods could value this raid-enabled third Pirate highly.
larger_swap_packages.why_not_selected: Seven isn't inherently worse, but Kari's guaranteed two-mana Pirate, menace, first strike and free non-Pirate Monkey attacker give utility across open defender states. Aerialist's raid timing can fail, and no honest finite rules fixture establishes higher overall power; retain as a credible meta variation.

larger_swap_packages.case_for_extra_swaps: Source-bound nine-replacement list broadens evasion, flying blockers and ward with Aerialist, Dreamcaller Siren and Brotherhood Regalia; this is a serious coherent higher-count package in ground-heavy interactive pods.
larger_swap_packages.why_not_selected: Losing Bident means fewer repeat draws over multiple Pirate hits; losing Open removes guaranteed X=3 unblock plus draws; losing instant Cannonade destroys the reactive defense against a non-Pirate swarm. More sources that might connect cannot compensate for sacrificing three distinct high-value functional roles in the actual 100.

open_ended_optimization_audit.quality_based_stop_reason: The count-independent stopping reason is that the selected full 100 preserves the highest-value commander-specific mix among seven tested physical source lists: three Pirate theft connections, reliable fast colored mana, repeatable multi-attacker card draw, precisely paid unblock combat and uniquely instant defensive non-Pirate damage. Seven and nine replacements were genuinely constructed and compared; they increase conditional evasion at the expense of Kari's effective combat abilities, Bident's repeat drawing, Open's guaranteed X=3 unblock/draw and Fiery Cannonade's instant protection. Without inventing multiplayer outcome statistics, there is no defensible marginal improvement from those extra swaps. Review can reopen for new material evidence, not a higher count for its own sake.
